Omar Ghosh: Hey team—my demo started hitting 429s around 10:11am PST. We're on the Free plan and have ~8 concurrent generator calls. Any quick lift options?
Maya (Support): Sorry about that, Omar. Can you paste the 429 response headers (if present) and the request pattern? We can check for a temporary burst but need usage window and org id.
Omar Ghosh: Org ID: org_01H3_example. Session id: sess-77. Sample response header: HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-RateLimit-Limit: 120
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1718378400
Body: {"error":"rate limit exceeded","code":"rate_limit"}
Maya (Support): Thanks — that looks like a per-minute request cap. Free plan has stricter caps. Quick mitigations: 1) reduce concurrency to 2-3, 2) add exponential backoff + jitter on 429s, 3) use streaming to reduce token spikes. We can also open a one-time temporary uplift request with Sales for demo hours.
Omar Ghosh: If Sales approves a temporary uplift, how fast does that go live? Demo is tonight.
Raj (Sales): We can approve a short-term uplift (adds +200 req/min) for up to 48h once we have org + billing contact + CC on file. I'll need invoice handle or PO. Ping me the billing email and I'll route for express approval.
Omar Ghosh: Billing email: billing@acme-apps.com. No PO, CC on file is limited. Is a trial credit possible instead?
Maya (Support): We can't change plan caps directly from Support. We can request an exception; for billing changes Sales needs to sign off. Meanwhile, if you share a short repro code we can suggest rate-limiting in client.
Omar Ghosh: Repro snippet:
```
for i in range(0, 50):
  payload = {"model":"gpt-4-mini","input":"short prompt"}
  requests.post(API_URL, headers=AUTH, json=payload)
```
Maya (Support): Two quick code tips: 1) batch requests where possible, 2) add a token-bucket limiter client-side: limit concurrent workers to 3 and sleep when you see 429 with Retry-After header. Also honor any Retry-After or rate limit headers.
Priya (Oncall): Also check that you're not mixing embeddings + generation at the same time which can spike token accounting. If you can route non-critical jobs to off-peak hours that helps.
Omar Ghosh: Sounds good. Raj — any chance for tonight?
Raj (Sales): I'll escalate. If you can confirm CC or emergency card, we can provision a temporary uplift within a couple hours. Otherwise we'll schedule for tomorrow AM. For compliance I need the billing contact and expected QPS/reqs you need.
Omar Ghosh: QPS ~3, peak concurrent requests 12 during demo. Expected tokens ~150k over 1 hour.
Raj (Sales): Got it. I submitted request with ops tag for 48h +200 req/min. Ticket #S-4529. ETA ~2h pending billing.
Maya (Support): I'll monitor logs and enable a temporary fallback policy to an older model if uplift not approved (auto-degrade to gpt-4-small). That avoids hard failures and preserves UX.
BillingBot: Billing hold detected on org_01H3_example — missing billing address. This may block express uplift.
Omar Ghosh: Oh — I'll add billing address now.
(30m later)
Raj (Sales): Update — billing verified, uplift approved for 36h starting 1718378400. Please verify traffic after 10pm PST.
Omar Ghosh: Confirmed — demo ran, no 429s. Thanks all :tada:
Maya (Support): Closing loop — created internal note with mitigation checklist and link to ops ticket S-4529. Reach out if you need extension.
Priya (Oncall): For long term, consider Dedicated plan or reserved burst add-on. Happy to connect on sizing.
Omar Ghosh: Will do. Thanks everyone.
